messages:
alex.hart: hey all — first week! trying to kubectl into my dev namespace but I get "Error from server (Forbidden): namespaces \"alex-dev\" is forbidden: User \"...\" cannot get resource \"namespaces\"". anyone know who to ping?

lina: welcome! :tada: run `redwood-kube-login` then `kubectl config get-contexts` — your namespace should be set to alex-dev if the onboarding role was applied. did you use the onboarding link in the new-hires guide?

alex.hart: ran `redwood-kube-login`, shows context rwd-dev-us-west, but `kubectl get pods -n alex-dev` => Forbidden.

jen.eng-infra: pinging infra. @alex.hart do `kubectl auth can-i get pods --namespace=alex-dev` and paste output. also paste `kubectl config view --minify -o jsonpath='{.contexts[0].context.namespace}'`.

alex.hart: `kubectl auth can-i get pods --namespace=alex-dev` -> no
`kubectl config view --minify -o jsonpath='{.contexts[0].context.namespace}'` -> <empty>

jen.eng-infra: ok that means your context doesn't have namespace bound or your user lacks RBAC in that ns. two quick options:
1) locally set the namespace so you don't need -n each time: `kubectl config set-context --current --namespace=alex-dev`
2) if you need permissions, we'll create a RoleBinding to give view access. i'll open a request now.

infra-bot: Created request INF-2024-317: assign view role to user alex.hart in namespace alex-dev. Assignee: jen.eng-infra

jen.eng-infra: created RoleBinding: `kubectl create rolebinding rb-onboard-alex --namespace=alex-dev --clusterrole=view --user=alex.hart` — this gives read-only access to resources in alex-dev. if you need edit rights, reply with why and i'll escalate.

mike.sre: quick note: for workloads we prefer serviceaccounts, but for interactive dev access user rolebindings are fine. also you can set your default namespace in kubeconfig (see above) to avoid repeating -n.

alex.hart: ran `kubectl get pods -n alex-dev` again and now it lists pods, thanks :raised_hands:

lina: awesome — tag me if you need registry creds, port-forward help, or a mentor for infra stuff this week.

alex.hart: one more quick q: how long do RBAC bindings last? temporary or permanent?

jen.eng-infra: by default permanent until removed. for onboarding we annotate with `onboard-expires=YYYY-MM-DD` and we usually revoke after 30 days unless you request extension. if you want auto-expiry open a ticket and say how long.

alex.hart: got it. closing thread — thanks everyone!
